_note: Body expression (pepin.expression): the gesture engine and the speaker gaze, run inside the voice cascade on the laptop. The atoms, compositions, taught poses and idle layers are config/animation.json; the arm's caps, limits and rest pose, which the board enforces, are config/arm.json's motion block; the face finder's detector is config/face_sensor.json's. Every number here is a design default until a line says MEASURED.

flags.note: The features' switches at the cascade's start; while it runs: scripts/voice_cascade.py switch --flag gestures=on (data/voice/control.json's flags, answered in control.jsonl). Switching a feature on re-reads this file and config/animation.json. gestures: every gesture and idle layer of every part (arm, head overlays, face cues, eyes, wheels); off, markers are still taken out of the speech and nothing moves. speaker_gaze: the head's base layer on the person and its turn of the wheels. doze: outside a conversation the face dozes (the doze block below; pepin.expression.doze).

timing.note: The word clock (pepin.expression.forecast) and the scheduler's send rule (pepin.expression.schedule). A marker's word is heard: the reply's first part tts_first_s after its text went to the voice (the first chunk's p10, 0.10 s: a stroke errs early, the free side; MEASURED p50 0.15) or where the part before it ends, then lead_silence_s (the voice's leading silence, MEASURED p50 0.16, p10 0.12, p90 0.30) and the word's first vowel at its share of the rest of the part, the part's length char_s a character (MEASURED 0.096 per reply, 0.089 on 2026-10-12) until this conversation's spoken parts give their running median; exact from the part's first chunk on, the prosody's stressed nucleus once its audio is analysed; audio_lag_s later on the speaker (the board's aplay start, config/face.json's lipsync start_latency_s 0.12, unmeasured, plus the WiFi hop). Each clip is sent at the last moment that lands its stroke stroke_bias_s from the vowel (negative: before; early is free, late costs recall). A word- or phrase-bound stroke is never later than stroke_late_s (past it: a smaller version, the head and face, or nothing); late_s: how late an utterance-bound one (today's feelings) may still land, inside the speech. short_s: an arm or wheels motion longer than this plays only when the speech ahead covers it. phrase_slide_s: how much later a phrase-bound mark may slide to one of the next two words. after_s: a tail (the laugh's rock, bound after its sentence's start) goes while its stroke still lands within this much speech after that start, inside the reply's speech. overrun_s (1.5, 0..3): how far a gesture's arm or wheels may run past the end of the speech known after its stroke (the fed audio as it is, 0.7 of a forecast), every composition alike; 2026-10-14, Artem: no special case for the wave, a lone «Привет!» (1.3 s of the greeting's hold after its stroke) must wave; 0.5 s, hello and bye 1 s before. poll_s: how often the engine looks at a waiting clip.

units.note: An arm unit (pepin.expression.schedule): a stroke with the next arm stroke due within hold_s after its end holds its last pose (the board's then: hold, under config/arm.json's hold_max_s 3) and the next plans from that pose instead of rest; at most strokes in one unit; a hold not taken lapses and the board rests the arm by itself.

layers.note: fade_s: per part, how long a layer change eases (the face in 0.1 s, the body in 0.35 s: Disney's bipedal character); the arm's is the board's own way to rest at its caps. The person starting to speak fades the gesture layer of every part, even while the robot is silent, but a gesture of finish (a greeting, a farewell) already past its stroke and ending within finish_s plays out. idle_resume_s: quiet on a part after a gesture before its idle layer plays again; idle_after_speech_s: no idle motion this soon after anyone spoke (an idle entry's own after_speech_s in config/animation.json wins: 0 lets a breath follow a reply at once). face_hold_s: how long a {face:NAME} marker's expression holds. head_seen_s: a gesture takes the head only while the speaker gaze tracks a person it saw within this (frames come at 1 Hz while the robot speaks: 1.2 s is one missed frame's margin; with the gaze off, no rule). seed: null draws a fresh seed for each performance (logged with it); a number makes every performance repeat (the bench). arm_past_arc: the arm waits while the person engaged stands past the forward arc (a body turn to come); off since 2026-10-14 (Artem: it held the arm for a person a room away).

caps.note: What the brain's markers and the robot's moments may play (a tool or scripts/gesture.py, which a person asked for, is never capped); a marker over a cap is dropped and logged. per_part: gestures in one voice part (a sentence, or a clause a style cut); per_reply (3, gesticulation DESIGN.md 5.5), per_minute: of all gestures; arm_per_minute: gestures with the arm (over it the rest of the gesture plays without the arm). accents ({!}, the accent): outside every count above, at most accent_per_part in a part (it replaces that sentence's pulse nod). series (count): the items of one reply count once, as its first: the later ones pass per_part, per_reply, per_minute and arm_per_minute (one unit of the arm). intent_per_minute: an intent's own; a composition's cooldown_s (config/animation.json) between two of its own with the same argument ({point:you} and {point:printer} are two). The person's laugh (laughter, a regex on what Whisper read, within laughter_s) waives the caps of laughter_waives. From expressive_motion.md: a person telling a story makes ~4 gestures a minute; no study gives an annoyance threshold: these are starting knobs. atoms_counted (2026-10-14): false, a mark of an atom's auto-wrapper (a single basic move: {head_nod}, {gripper_click:2}) counts under per_part alone, never toward per_reply, per_minute or arm_per_minute; true counts it as any composition's.

voice_stats.measured: MEASURED 2026-10-12 on qwen3-1.7b's voice, 10-10/11 (scratch/gesticulation_1012/pulse_signal.py); the listener's own band measure gives -28.9 +- 5.5, 0.147 +- 0.115, 1.8 +- 3.3 (scratch/gesticulation_alive/offline_pulse.py)

pulse.note: The body while the robot speaks, from its own voice's audio (pepin.expression.prosody finds the nuclei and the melody, pepin.expression.listeners turns them into requests); no flag: it rides gestures. Every accent is an ensemble, the book's own composition by its strength (config/animation.json pulse_weak, pulse_strong, pulse_peak: their nods', beats' and rocks' sizes are the book's), each part where it is free and its lead covers its way. melody_deg_per_st (0.2, 0.05..0.5): the head's tilt a semitone of the voice's pitch round the part's median, up with the pitch. melody_max_deg (0.9, 0..1.5; 0: no melody): the melody's most; within the arbiter's gaze.clip_still_deg (2.0, config/knobs.json) it never blinds the head. melody_cutoff_hz (0.5, 0.25..2.0): the contour's low-pass; 0.5 since 2026-10-13 evening (1.0 before): only the phrase's rise and fall reach the head, a syllable's flutter does not. melody_key_gap_s (1.0, 0.5..2.0): the melody's keys at least this far apart, each written with the gentlest speed and ramp that land it on time so the servo glides between them (2026-10-13: +-0.9 deg as keys every 0.25 s at the tilt's full ramp read as a jerky head; the idle layer's keys glide since; 1.0 since the evening, 0.5 before: a key every 0.5 s, each a glide that starts and ends at rest, read to Artem as a floating drift, a bug; a key a second or more is one slow motion, and under the arbiter's rule of writing a key only once the head has settled a sparse stream loses none of them to the holder's moves). beat_z (2.0, 1..4): an accent on a nucleus whose prominence (band level + voiced length + pitch, each a z over voice_stats) reaches this: on a stressed vowel of a content word 72 % (any nucleus 44 %), in 38 % of sentences. strong_z (3.0, beat_z..6): from here an accent is pulse_strong (the nod, the wrist's beat with the arm up, the cart's 1 cm rock), and the reply's strongest known (once a reply) pulse_peak (all three bigger); under it pulse_weak; MEASURED 2026-10-12/13: the 24 accents played live had z 2.2..5.1, median 2.9 (deciles 2.2, 2.4, 2.6, 2.8, 2.9, 3.0, 3.3, 3.6, 5.1). beat_gap_s (2.0, 1..5): an accent's nod at least this long after any head stroke. beats_per_minute (12, 0..30; 0: no accent nods). beat_lead_min_s (0.30, 0.30..1.0): no nod with less lead than this, nor than its own preparation (its bottom 0.2 s after its first move at the earliest, plus parts.head.latency_s); an accent decides when the lead of the slowest part it wants is about to run out (the wheels' rock: ~1 s at wheels.speed_scale 0.4). mark_gap_s (0.6, 0..2): never a nod within this of a marker's head stroke (a part with a marker of the brain's gets no accent at all). wrist_beat_p (0.5, 0..1): a weak accent's share with the wrist's beat while a unit holds the arm up (a strong one beats always); the beat rides the held pose and keeps the rest of its hold; no unit, no beat. wheel_accent_share (0.5, 0..1; 0: no sway): the weak accents carrying the cart's 0.5 cm sway, steady (every second one at 0.5, the next free one when the cart was busy), the strong ones' 1 cm rock besides; the cart takes a rock only once its last motion has ended and settled, never during the gaze's body turn (the one thing that outranks the pulse's wheels) or a drive. laugh_run (3, 2..8; 0: never), laugh_gap_s ([0.2, 0.4]): a run of this many accents this far apart in a part is the voice laughing: each of its accents asks for pulse_laugh (the cart's rock with the happy face, a bob of the head), the cart taking the next one once its rock is over (about one a second and a half at speed 0.4: a laugh's 3-5 Hz is out of the wheels' reach); DESIGN DEFAULT: the laughs logged on 2026-10-13 had syllables at z 3.8..13.1 (Mva-ha-ha), 0.1..4.0 (Ha-ha-ha, slow) and under 0 (a quiet sinister one), their spacing unlogged. arm_up_min_sentences (2, 1..6; 0: never): a reply with this many parts with words at the voice (a sentence, or a clause a style cut; their text, before their sound) raises the arm once to the book's ready within its next half second of speech (with 1 s of its speech known after it) and holds it there while it goes on: the hold reaches 0.5 s past the audio known, sent again before it lapses (at most config/arm.json's hold_max_s at a time), a mark plans from it and the arm comes back to ready after the mark, the accents' beats ride it, and while nothing moves it the arm breathes in every joint (config/animation.json's breath layer; the book's arm_sway, the wrist alone, when the book has no breath for the arm); to rest when the person speaks, at the reply's end or cut, for the body's turn, and when a part in a quiet style begins. arm_up_caps_share (0.3, 0.1..1.0): the share of config/arm.json's caps the posture's raise runs at, and its way down at the reply's end or cut (the arm's own slow trajectory to rest; the person's start and the body's turn keep the board's quick way, the arm clears out); 0.3 since 2026-10-13 evening (0.5 before, the raise 0.78 s at 109 deg/s peak: Artem, the raise is LOUD, the gesticulation after it quiet; the servos whine with speed): rest to ready 1.3 s at 66 deg/s peak, where the quiet beats live; the posture rises only with a second of speech known after it, so a slow raise costs nothing but a later start, and short and quick is a stroke's rule, not a posture's. The cart rocks under the raised arm (one body: neither waits for the other). voice_stats: the voice's nuclei, (mean, standard deviation) each, refitted per voice.

moments.question: \?|^\W*(?:(?:а|и|ну)\W+)?(?:кто|где|когда|почему|зачем|куда|откуда|сколько|разве|неужели)\b
moments.note: The robot's moments between turns and while the person speaks (pepin.expression.listeners); no flag: they ride gestures; read again at each conversation's open. The breath while the robot is silent is config/animation.json's looping idle entry (its atom breath: amp_deg 1.0 at 0.25 Hz; over gaze.clip_still_deg it would blind the head while it breathes). head_gap_s (1.0, 0.5..3.0): every discrete head stroke at least this far from the one before (a held look's return counts), so head moves never pile up at a turn's edge; the reply's yes/no nod keeps it too. think_glance_s (0.8, 0.5..1.5): the thinking glance when the turn closed and no reply audio came this long; think_p (0.75, 0..1); think_deg ([8, 15], 4..20); think_back_s ([0.5, 1.3]): back this far into the reply as this conversation's waits predict it (the first wait 1.95 s, MEASURED p50); think_dirs: up, down, aside by weight, never the same way twice running (Andrist et al. 2013). aversion_reply_s (6.0, 3..20): a reply with this much audio known looks away once, aversion_deg ([5, 8]) aside or down for aversion_s ([1.5, 2.0]) at an inner pause, back at least end_gaze_s (2.4) before its audio ends. listener_nod_p (0.6, 0..1), listener_gap_s (5, 2..20), listener_min_speech_s (2.0, 0.5..5): at the ears' pause inside the person's speech, never while their last words were a question, the book's listen_nod: its nod with listener_nod_p. ack_nod_p (0.3, 0..1), ack_min_s (1.5, 0.5..5): predict_delay_s (0.2, 0..1) after the close of a statement (question: their words' question mark or a question word first), once a turn, never with a greeting, the book's ack_nod: its nod with ack_nod_p. nod_rock_p (0.3, 0..1; 0: never): either nod's ensemble rocks the cart 0.5 cm (the book's body_rock at its low end) with this chance, drawn apart from the nod's, where the cart is free (it may come a little after the nod); the nods' sizes are the book's. greeting (a regex on the person's words; a goodbye is the voice loop's own rule): a hello or a bye gets neither the acknowledgement nor the thinking glance; the wave is the brain's own {greeting} or {farewell} on its word, never the engine's (2026-10-14, Artem: no scripted start). The brain's {laugh} is its composition, every part together (the face, the head thrown back, the gripper's click, the cart's rock); the voice's laughing sound rocks the cart too (pulse.laugh_run). smile_s (2.0): the face's smile at the attention engine's first clear face of the conversation (speaker.smile null leaves the engine the face's one writer). listen_shift_deg (0.0, 0..2; 0: off): a still shift of the head every listen_shift_s ([6, 12]) while the person speaks, for the bench.

quiet.note: When only the melody, the breath and the face move (no nods, no glances, no arm, no wheels; a person's ask still plays whole): a reply in one of styles, the local hours from hours[0] to hours[1] (23..8; equal: never), or the person's last utterance peaking under peak_db dBFS (-30; their p10 / p50 / p90 were -24 / -14 / -8, MEASURED 10-11/12). Each change is a quiet event in the conversation's events.jsonl with its reason.

arm.note: latency_s: the WiFi hop and the board's next tick. speed_scale: every arm clip's time stretched by 1/speed_scale and the servos' profile capped by it; 0.2 for the first live test; 1.0 since 2026-10-12 evening on Artem's word (hello, bye and evil_click played at 1.0 by hand; the voice loop at 0.2 read as slow motion). knot_hz: the knots a clip is sampled into (the board interpolates between them on its 50 Hz tick).

head.note: latency_s: the door's HTTP, the arbiter's step and the neck_target hop.

face.note: latency_s: the head server's hop; its 280 ms tween (config/face.json timing) starts after it.

eyes.note: latency_s: the head server's hop (the same as the face's); the firmware's 160 ms tween into an override (config/face.json eyes.timing.override_ms) starts after it.

finder.note: THE SNAPSHOT PATH's finder (vision.source snapshot, the way round a broken perception service): on the default path the perception service detects (config/models.json's perception block) and this block is not read. Where the speaker gaze's face detector (SCRFD, det_10g) runs: compute_units is CoreML's CPUAndNeuralEngine (the CPU and the Neural Engine, never the GPU, where the voice's Qwen3-TTS runs: on 2026-10-12 the voice's first chunk took 230-400 ms with the detector free to use the GPU against 100-150 ms without the gaze), ALL (CoreML chooses, the GPU included: as before), CPUAndGPU, or CPU (onnxruntime's own CPU provider); a network CoreML refuses runs on the CPU, said once in the log. bodies: the people detector beside the face detector, vision (Apple Vision's VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest, on the Neural Engine: 3.0 ms median at 800x600, +110-125 MB, MEASURED 2026-10-12 with scratch/gaze/vision_probe.swift; needs pyobjc-framework-Vision: uv add --group macos pyobjc-framework-Vision, without it the finder says so once and runs faces only) or none. body_head_frac: an upright person's head is this share of their box's height below its top (a lying person's box: its middle; a box the frame's top edge cuts: that edge).

wheels.note: The wheels' expressive motions (pepin.expression.wheels: the speaker gaze's turn toward a person past the forward arc (speaker.arc_deg), the gestures' body atoms): twist lines from this Mac to the board's base server over its own link (the measured motions' method, never Nav2), judged by the base server's wheel odometry; nothing new runs on the board. Read again at every motion (the gesture engine reads speed_scale when gestures switch on: it stretches the body's clips). max_turn_deg: the most one request turns (more is refused, never clamped); step_deg: a turn tells its progress every step_deg (the speaker gaze reads the odometry's heading itself ten times a second while a turn runs); max_rock_m: the most a rock or a body clip drives. backoff_m, backoff_deg: the one recovery, one rule for every turn that ends short (it stalls, or the marks block its arc): a straight step of backoff_m (default 0.02, above 0 and at most max_rock_m) away from the obstacle mark nearest the footprint, forward unless that mark lies ahead of the footprint's middle (forward with no mark: ahead is where the camera and the ToF look), checked like any leg; when that step is blocked or stalls too, a turn of backoff_deg (default 10, above 0 and at most max_turn_deg; the rear corners move 7 cm) back the other way instead; then the rest of the turn once more, and if that ends short too it gives up (the head looks as far as it reaches). The cart never ends a request more than max_turn_deg from the heading it began at. A halt, someone else's command, a drive or a refused check never recovers or retries. speed_scale: every cap below times it (ramps times its square, as a clip stretched by 1/speed_scale moves); 0.4 (2026-10-12, Artem: the turn toward a call from behind was too slow at 0.2), 1.0 (2026-10-13, Artem: the 30 deg turn at 0.4 was slow and timid; the whole turn in one request, max_turn_deg 180, the rate 45 deg/s, the ramp 180 deg/s^2 = 3.1 rad/s^2, the book's body clips at their own speed), raised by Artem's word. yaw_rate_deg_s, yaw_acc_deg_s2: the turn's top rate and ramp at speed 1 (30 deg/s swings the rear corners, 0.41 m out, at 0.21 m/s; a wheel rim at 0.14 m/s of config/base.json's 0.30); the ramp 360 makes the turn decisive rather than cautious: at speed 0.4 the rate is 12 deg/s, reached in 0.21 s at 57.6 deg/s^2 (1.0 rad/s^2, the ramp Nav2's rotate-to-heading uses on this cart, ros/params/nav2_params.yaml max_angular_accel), so a 30 deg turn's profile is 2.7 s (6.7 s at 0.2 and 90; on the simulated base 2.5 s against 5.3: scratch/gaze/turn_time.py), plus 0.1-0.6 s of checks before the first twist; at a speed_scale over 0.56 the ramp passes the velocity smoother's 2.0 rad/s^2 (lower it with the scale); speed_m_s, acc_m_s2: a straight leg's (the rock, the back-off). MEASURED 2026-10-13 on the servo bus tap (five body turns at 45 deg/s, the ramp 180 asked): the cart ramps at 100-109 deg/s^2 up and 98-109 down whatever is asked, the wheel servos' own Acceleration (50 units, 5000 ticks/s^2: 0.48 m/s^2 at the rim, 101 deg/s^2 of yaw on the 0.544 m track), so 180 asked only runs the command ahead of the cart for the first 0.3 s (harmless: the odometry judges; the stall judge saw 0.43 of the commanded motion in the first 0.5 s against its 0.33 floor); a twist written to the bus moves the cart's rate 0.11-0.19 s later, the loop's own read-to-write 0.04 s. yaw_brake_deg_s2 (100, MEASURED above): the ramp the cart really brakes at; a turn's braking is planned on the lesser of it and the ramp asked at the scale. lead_s (0.17, MEASURED above: the servos' 0.11-0.19 after the bus write, median 0.15, plus the twist's way to the bus, 0.01-0.02): the transport delay from a twist's sending to the cart's answer, so what the cart does over the next lead_s is what was sent over the last; every tick brakes from where the cart will be when its twist takes effect (the twists in flight added to the newest line's place) and sends the zero once that place is within half of settle_deg, the cart's own last brake running the other half; the stall judge holds the cart to the twists in force a lead earlier, not to those still in flight (on the simulated cart the five turns land within +-2 deg for a true delay of 0.11-0.19 s and +3.4..+5.1 at 0.23).  Before these (the ramp 180 and a lead of 0.06 s planned on the command's own speed) the five turns landed +6.4..+8.1 deg past the ask: 149.7 asked, 157.8 turned; -40.9 -> -48.5; -52.6 -> -60.2; -76.1 -> -84.1; -72.4 -> -79.2, each at 45 deg/s until 0.15 s after the first braking twist, then 9-10 deg of the servos' own braking; the 2 cm back-off steps went 2.9-3.2 cm for the same lead. settle_deg, settle_m: a leg this close to its target (or past it) is done. clearance_m: the swept footprint (config/base.json) must keep this far from every obstacle mark it moves toward (depth_fusion's /depth_marks through the goal server: the voxel volume's lidar, camera depth and ToF, remembered round the cart, 0.15-1.3 m above the floor out to 3 m; lower things are not seen; a bearing the volume holds nothing on blocks nothing); 0.5 means nobody within half a metre of the swept cart. marks_age_s: older marks (by their own stamp) are no marks, and no marks refuses every motion (depth_fusion down: the reason in the wheels' line, never the raw scan instead); 1.5 s because a slice carries the stamp of the observation that triggered it, a camera frame's among them, and on the drive bags of 2026-10-07..09 a request ten times a second met marks p50 0.31, p99 1.03, max 1.46 s old (0.5 would refuse 17 % of the checks; the gaps between slices p50 0.22, max 0.59 s): it catches a silent depth_fusion, not an old stamp. stall_s: a leg that makes less than a third of its commanded motion over this long is stalled. stop_hold_s: after someone else's stop during a motion (the red button, the teleop's stop) every motion is refused this long. latency_s: from a gesture's cue to the first motion (the goal server's first answer, the WiFi). clearance_check: the arc and the way checked against the obstacle marks before and during a motion (off since 2026-10-14, Artem: the marks 0.3 m ahead, the dock on the base and his own legs when near, refused 19 of 21 body turns; off, a turn runs on the odometry alone and the marks' age is not read).

doa.mac_measured: MEASURED 2026-10-14 (ros/tools/doa_calibrate.py --source mac): front 182, left 76, behind 7, right 285 deg; quarter-turn misses +0, +17, -5, -12
doa.measured: MEASURED 2026-10-12 (ros/tools/doa_calibrate.py): front 170, left 106, behind 343, right 278 deg; quarter-turn misses +0, -26, +7, -18
doa.note: The XVF3800 sits on the cart's front-left (where the left arm would be), not on the head. readings: the array's angle (0..359, 0 toward its USB-C side) of a voice 1.5 m in front of, left of, behind and right of the cart; the bearing is interpolated between them (front, left, behind, right are 0, +90, 180, -90 deg exactly), which absorbs the off-centre array's uneven quarters. front_deg and sign (+1 when the angle grows toward the cart's left, -1 toward its right) alone turn the angle by an offset when the four are not all known. ros/tools/doa_calibrate.py --write measures and writes all of it (one phrase three times at each place; it refuses a reading nearer another quarter than its own); front_deg and sign null and no readings: the gaze orients by faces alone (the head tilts to seek_tilt_deg where it points and looks for a face). window_s: the speech-flagged readings of the utterance's last window_s (the utterance's end mapped onto the board's clock by the newest reading) are averaged (circular mean) into its bearing; fewer than min_speech of them (about 10 a second arrive) and the voice has no bearing. doa_tags, voice_p_min (2026-10-14): which readings are the person's voice (pepin.expression.doa, one rule for the utterance's bearing, the follow and the counts above): silero, the array's speech flag AND the ears' Silero probability around the reading (the max within 0.1 s; barge_in.vad_model, the ears' own model, no second instance) of at least voice_p_min AND not the robot's own speech (its spans and 0.3 s of echo) AND not the start of the robot's own wheels' turn (the first 0.5 s of a turn of the gaze's own); chip, the array's flag AND not the robot's own speech (as before). The array's flag is its firmware's energy and spectrum thresholds: the day's six 'no words' lines (the neck's and the wheels' noise) came with 86 of 87 readings flagged. MEASURED 2026-10-14 (scratch/gaze/doa_silero.py, the day's 12 conversations): the person's flagged readings Silero 0.5 or more 74 % (median 0.99), the 'no words' lines' 42 % (median 0.28); readings every 0.1 s in the neck's own motion with nobody speaking 2.5 %, in the wheels' 25 % (their start 0.2-0.4 s after the command 89 %, hence the motion tag; from 0.5 s on 0-6 %, the room's 3-5 %); in the bearing window the six 'no words' lines keep 0-5 readings of 9-11 (none reaches 6), 17 of 20 worded lines keep 6 or more (doa_min_speech; voice_p_min 0.3 keeps 18; 0.3 with a 0.15 s window 20, but one 'no words' line then reaches 7; the three short of it at 0.5: 2, 4 and 5). Without the ears' Silero (barge_in.detector level) the silero rule hears nobody (a line at each wake says so): doa_tags chip then. direction, mac_voice_p_min, mac_peak_ratio, mac_reading_s, mac_readings (2026-10-14): whose readings the gaze reads. chip: the array's own, as above. mac: the Mac's own from the four raw microphones (pepin.audio_doa; needs the 6-channel firmware and raw_mics in config/audio.json; while no raw frames come the chip's are read and a line says so once each way): SRP-PHAT over the array's geometry on the chunks Silero calls voice (mac_voice_p_min: the chunk's probability, the ears' own series), every source peak at least mac_peak_ratio of the chunk's strongest kept beside the reading (0.6: on the synthetic stream a second voice reads 0.88-0.95 of the strongest, the square's mirror lobe 0.36, the alias lobes 0.2-0.36) and fed to the register of voices (gaze_sources: id, bearing, age, strength; the engaged person is one of them, the others keep their last bearing; nobody is engaged from it), one reading per mac_reading_s (0.1: the chip's cadence, so min_speech, doa_min_speech and follow_min_speech keep their meaning; 0.032 is one per chunk). The silero/chip rule above applies to the Mac's readings unchanged (their flag is Silero's at the chunk). mac_readings: the Mac's own four quarter readings (its angles are the geometry's frame of config/audio.json, 0 along +x, not the chip's), ros/tools/doa_calibrate.py --source mac --write; all null: the chip's readings stand in for the Mac's angles, an estimate. NOT MEASURED on the robot yet (the 6-channel firmware is to be flashed); the synthetic stream gives a clean wave its grid degree and one 32 ms chunk at 0 dB of independent noise per mic a median 2.5 deg off (p90 6, max 12 of 40; at -6 dB it breaks down) (tests/unit/test_audio_doa.py); scratch/gaze/mac_doa_bench.py compares the Mac's angle with the chip's over a session.

speaker.note: The speaker gaze is one engine (pepin.expression.tracker): stimuli (the array's DOA stream with the robot's own speaking spans cut out, utterances, one head-camera frame of faces and people's boxes) place a few PEOPLE TRACKS (pepin.expression.tracks), the POLICY engages the person speaking (pepin.expression.policy) and the head moves in one eased aim, pan and tilt together. MOTION: turn_speed_deg_s, turn_acc_deg_s2, adjust_acc_deg_s2: every aim is an angles look with the servo's own trapezoid as its ease (neck_target's speed_deg_s and acc_deg_s2): a TURN to a new person at turn_acc_deg_s2 (650: 20 deg in 0.35 s, 60 deg in 0.61 s, peaks 114 and 198 deg/s, a human head's coarse turn), an ADJUSTMENT (onto the face, a person moving, the voice followed, the seek's stops, the residue of the body's turn) at adjust_acc_deg_s2 (400: 6 deg in 0.25 s, 20 deg in 0.45 s, 40 deg in 0.63 s); both capped at turn_speed_deg_s; while the body turns, the GLIDE (glide_ahead_s, glide_gain below); the board keeps the tilt's own 600 deg/s^2 ramp under them, so a combined move arcs; 0 for a ramp: the arbiter's saccade or slow speed instead (as before 2026-10-12). THE BODY, one rule: arc_deg (60 since 2026-10-13: +-30 deg of the cart's nose, Artem: face the person; 160 on 2026-10-12): the head alone serves any bearing within this forward arc; the person engaged past it turns the body toward them (to face them, at most wheels.max_turn_deg a request, asked again while they are still past it: 150 deg is one request of 150 since 2026-10-13, Artem: the 30 deg chunks left him looked at sideways), the wheels started before the head's aim and neither waiting for the other (the head, the fast one, arrives first); not during a check, and while the wheels cannot (a refused check, a stall, a blocked arc, the caps) the head alone stays on the person as far as it reaches: a refusal or a cut turn is asked again at the person's next utterance, a turn that moved the cart and still fell short not again for that person in the conversation (no creeping back-offs); after a tool's drive or turn not until the person's next words begun after it ended (2026-10-14, Artem: a turn on command waits for the first phrase; turn(180) and turn(printer) were undone by this rule seconds later), the head tracking them meanwhile. The person speaking never stops it (it is the base layer, as the head's tracking is; the gestures' motions do stop). THE FRAME: the people's bearings are kept in the cart's frame at the newest heading of the wheels' odometry (the base server's state lines, on the board's clock, whoever turned the cart): a turn since is taken off every person, off each of the array's readings by its own stamp (an utterance spoken across a turn gives the bearing the person has now; gaze_doa rows then carry the degrees taken off), and the head KEEPS the person as the body comes round under it (a seek's stop keeps its place in the room): the arbiter answers an aim once the head has settled on it, and a re-aim per odometry tick waiting for that answer was a stop-and-go move each (2026-10-13, the 158 deg turn: five moves of 20-25 deg with 0.14 s of standing between, the head 20-35 deg behind the person in the room throughout, +-5 deg of saw-tooth; Artem: the chicken's head, locked on the target while the body comes round), so while the wheels turn every aim goes out without waiting (a short thread makes the door's call, its answer comes back through the machine's inbox; a newer aim preempts the older at the arbiter and the base server's mover takes it in flight) and every 0.1 s the aim is the person's pan glide_ahead_s (0.2, 0..0.5: the head's own latency 0.1 and one tick; DESIGN DEFAULT) ahead at the body's measured rate, with a speed ceiling of glide_gain (2.0, 1..4; DESIGN DEFAULT: the head catches up a lag at the body's rate again, 20 deg/s at least as the body comes to rest) times that rate on the adjustment's ramp: the head follows a target always a little ahead and never stops to settle; the turn's end re-centres the residue as an adjustment. PEOPLE: a face gives a person's head aim; a body box (finder.bodies) an estimate of it (finder.body_head_frac), so a standing, sitting or lying person is aimed at without a face; a voice gives a bearing at the track's remembered tilt, seek_tilt_deg for a new one (+3: the faces seen on 2026-10-12 sat at +0.6..+6.3 deg, median +3.2; the picture is 59 deg tall, so a standing face at 1 m, -19 deg, is in it too). match_deg: a face or a body this near a person's bearing is that person; voice_match_deg: a voice this near is theirs (the array read 5-14 deg off the face at a normal level), else a new voice-only person. tilt_hysteresis_deg (12, 0..30): the person's tilt changes its source, a face's to a body box's estimate or back, only when the two differ by more than this (the pan follows the newest sighting either way; one source moves its own tilt freely); the head nodded between Artem's face and his box on 2026-10-12 (one switch logged stepped the tilt 10.5 deg: scratch/gaze/tilt_sources.py); a posture change (sitting down, standing up: 15-30 deg at 1-2 m) still moves it. DESIGN DEFAULT. seen_fresh_s: a person seen (face or body) this recently keeps their place against the voice; an older one takes the fresh voice's bearing and keeps its tilt (a stale place never wins over a fresh bearing). max_tracks, track_forget_s: people kept, and forgotten when unseen and unheard this long (kept across conversations for their tilt; a drive forgets them). WHOM: the robot's name always turns the head (a seek, no return); words from a person seen before switch at once; words from a voice with nobody seen there while someone seen is engaged make a check: one frame within verify_s there, back when nobody; with nobody engaged a seek. doa_min_speech, doa_min_dbfs: an utterance without words, with fewer speech-flagged readings, or a peak under doa_min_dbfs never moves the head, the name aside (2026-10-12: at -16 dBFS or louder the bearing was 5-14 deg off the face, n 8; at -20..-22 dBFS 28, 72 and 76 deg off in three of four, at -30 76 deg: scratch/gaze/doa_vs_face.py). An utterance overlapping the robot's speech keeps its clean readings (outside the robot's spans and 0.3 s after); fewer than doa_min_speech of them: it moves nothing. SEEK (the person engaged has a bearing, nobody is seen there): seek_frames frames seek_every_s apart at each place, first the voice of the last doa_follow_s (moved more than doa_moved_deg: go there), then seek_pan_deg outward of the bearing and as far inward at the same tilt (outward first: the three misses logged had the face further from the nose than the voice; 0 since 2026-10-13, Artem: no head sweep looking for a person, the head stays on the voice and the body turns to it (30 since 2026-10-14, Artem: the array's bearing is coarse, so the head looks a little past it and sweeps 30 deg back, the frames taken on the way; one frame covers ~80 deg, so 140 deg are seen)), then back to the voice; a person within seek_pan_deg + match_deg of the bearing is the one sought; no tilt sweep. FOLLOW: while the person speaks and nobody has seen them for seen_fresh_s the head follows the voice's clean speech readings of the last doa_follow_s (at least follow_min_speech of them), in steps over doa_moved_deg and at most follow_max_deg (a jump is a new voice, judged when its utterance ends). seek_min_face_px, track_min_face_px: faces from seek_min_face_px wide count near a person known and while seeking (a 0.15 m face is ~40 px at 2 m, ~26 px at 3 m in the raw eye; config/face_sensor.json); a new person needs track_min_face_px; a face under it is aimed at but not smiled at. Both are in the RECTIFIED left eye's pixels since 2026-10-12 (the perception service's records; fx 454.5 against the raw eye's 528 at the centre, so 28 and 40 became 24 and 34: the same distance for a centred face); off the axis the rectified picture is stretched, so a face there reads wider than in the raw eye (58 px against 49 at ~25 deg, scratch/perception_1012/eye_parity.py) and is counted from further away. On vision.source snapshot the widths are the raw eye's again and these thresholds admit faces ~14 % further than before. min_body_score: a body box scored under it is nobody (Vision scored the people of 2026-10-05's frames 0.55-0.76). track_hz: frames a second while the robot listens and the head is the speaker's and carries no gesture (a breath does not count), standing still until the person is tracked and moving or not once they are (since 2026-10-14: every record, each box placed with the head's pose at its frame's exposure stamp): one record of the perception service exposed after the head settled, or while tracking the next one (a loopback long poll; the service detects at its own detect_hz, config/models.json), or on vision.source snapshot a 42 KB snapshot (~45 ms of network wait), SCRFD on the Neural Engine (5.6 ms) and the body detector (3 ms) on the gaze's own thread; at the arbiter's door a still person costs 600 state reads and 30 renewals a minute and no aim. track_speaking_hz: the rate while the robot speaks (10 since 2026-10-14, Artem: at 1 the gaze lost a person walking; the detector is the perception service's, on the CPU and the Neural Engine, never the voice's GPU, at its own detect_hz whatever the gaze reads; 1.0 before). hold_for_voice: from a reply's first part going to the voice until its first chunk is with the player, no frame and no detection (2026-10-12: the first chunk took 230-400 ms with the gaze on, 100-150 without). lead_s, lead_max_deg: a moving person is aimed where they will be lead_s from now (their speed fitted over their sightings of the last 0.5 s at the frames' exposure stamps, pan only), at most lead_max_deg past the last sighting; since 2026-10-14 a person moving at least aim_min_deg within lead_s is pursued at every frame, the aims sent without waiting like the body's glide, at glide_gain times their speed (the tilt follows past refine_deg and never turns back within 0.2 s of its last turn: the arbiter's clip_max_hz 2.5). refine_deg: after a turn, a person further than this off the frame's centre is centred. deadband_deg: while tracking, a person standing this close to the centre moves nothing. saccade_over_deg: a correction larger than this is a turn, a smaller one an adjustment. aim_min_deg: an aim less than this from the last one is not written. face_lost_s, face_lost_frames: the person engaged is lost after face_lost_frames frames without them AND face_lost_s (the frames counted are the records the finder gave: a look that got none is no frame); the head then goes to their voice when it was heard while nothing saw them, else stays; frames go on. ttl_s, renew_s: the speaker's look lives ttl_s and is renewed every renew_s, so the head goes home within ttl_s of the cascade's end; a renewal that finds the look gone (a look the person asked for took the head) asks again, queued behind it. aim_wait_s: how long an aim waits for the arbiter's answer before it is taken as queued. smile (null as shipped: the gesture engine smiles at the first clear face, the face's one writer), smile_hold_s: a face's name brings back the gaze's own expression (source expression, through the head server) at the first clear face (track_min_face_px or more) of a conversation, once; smile_unseen: smile also when nobody is found. body_turn (2026-10-14, Artem: Nav2's Spin for the body's turn instead of the wheels' own executor): spin, the turn toward the person past the arc is one request of the whole bearing (at most wheels.max_turn_deg) to the goal server's spin, Nav2's Spin: one owner of turns in place (the turn tool's too), with its own collision check against the local costmap (it may refuse or abort beside furniture or on the dock), refused while any Nav2 goal runs or with the goal server's spin_requests off; the wheels' base link is opened at the request for the odometry's heading, which the people and the glide follow as before; a refusal waits for the person's next utterance, a spin that moved and fell short is not asked again for that person in the conversation. wheels: the expressive wheels executor of before (twists to the base server, the wheels block), kept for A/B.

doze.note: Dozing (flag doze; pepin.expression.doze, Artem 2026-10-15: sleepy as the default outside a conversation, a z now and then, so one sees it listens or dozes and waits to be called): with no conversation open and nothing happening for idle_after_s (no drive, no other source on the face: the head server's status names who holds a request), the face shows expression (sleepy: the eyes' doze effect and the mouth's z run in the firmware) as the standing request of the head server's source doze; a wake (the wake word opening a conversation, any of its moments, a drive, another source on the face, the flag off) lets it go at once and the head server's resting_expression shows. idle_after_s counts after the conversation's close (whose own idle close is config/voice_cascade.json's conversation.idle_close_s, 20 s).
